item.description: DigitalCommons@UTEP (The University of Texas at El Paso) — As data increasingly shapes participation in society, there is growing emphasis on preparing youth to engage with data through computer science education. item.title: Malaria in urban Ethiopia: anthropological insights for prevention and control in Jimma City, Ethiopia
item.description: Malaria Journal — Urban malaria is a rising public health threat driven by rapid urbanization and structural inequalities. However, little is known about the lived, socio-environmental dimensions of urban malaria in Jimma City. This study examines the socio-environmental and institutional factors influencing malaria prevention and control in Jimma City, southwest Oromia, Ethiopia. item.description: Research Square — Abstract Urban streets are fundamental public spaces that underpin residents’ daily non-motorized travel, and their on-street pedestrian environment and walkability directly shape people’s walking mode decisions and walking experiences. item.description: Research Square — Abstract Background KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) has experienced recurrent floods, with the April 2022 floods regarded as among the most devastating in South Africa’s recorded history. We examined how flood-related extreme weather events shaped healthcare utilisation, HIV treatment continuity and livelihood experiences among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in rural KwaZulu-Natal. item.description: Preprint / source unavailable — Climate adaptation has moved from the margins of environmental policy to the centre of public law, economic gov ernance and human-rights protection. The legal challenge is distinctive because adaptation has no single metric equivalent to tonnes of greenhouse gases. item.description: Research Square — Abstract Anticipatory Governance (AG) has emerged as a strategic approach for addressing uncertainty, systemic risk, and complexity in contemporary socio-technical systems. Methods A stratified random sample of 1,139 households was selected from three alternative housing areas: Al-Mahrousa ( n = 757), Ard El-Khayala ( n = 235), and Rawdat Al-Sayeda ( n = 147). item.description: Discover Public Health — Risky sexual behaviours, like non-spousal/non-cohabiting multiple partnerships (NSNCMP), increase the risk of STIs, HIV, and unintended pregnancies in Nigeria, especially among youth. Using the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, this study quantifies state-level sex differences in NSNCMP. item.title: Rethinking environmental justice through behavioural opportunity: developing a relational territorial vulnerability framework from IPSA-derived behavioural evidence
item.description: Environmental Impact Assessment Review — Environmental justice research has primarily explained health inequalities through environmental risks and resource distribution. Public spaces have similarly been assessed through quantity and accessibility, with planning interventions focused on optimizing resource allocation. item.description: Frontiers in Malaria — Introduction This study examines malaria epidemiology among populations engaged in illegal gold mining in Roraima, Brazil, to inform public health policy. item.description: Discover Public Health — Anemia during pregnancy remains a critical public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, contributing heavily to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. This study assessed the prevalence of anemia and its associated socioeconomic, dietary practices, and educational correlates among pregnant women registered for antenatal care (ANC) across government Urban Primary Health Centers (UPHCs) in Meerut City, India. item.description: International Journal of Health Geographics — Abstract Background Dengue has expanded markedly in Argentina, with Aedes aegypti now established in temperate provinces and successive epidemics culminating in a record outbreak in 2024. item.description: Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering — Introduction Lane detection is an essential feature of advanced driver assistance systems for reliable road scene perception. It allows the vehicle to determine the lane position and the orientation of its path within the lane. In recent years, deep learning has offered accurate approaches for lane detection in both the 2D image plane and 3D road coordinates. item.description: Frontiers in Public Health — Background As demographic ageing progresses, increasing attention has been paid to ensuring access to basic energy services for households with older members and understanding their potential vulnerability. item.description: Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution — Urban biodiversity loss is increasingly framed as a governance challenge with intertwined ecological and social dimensions, yet little is known about who participates in local biodiversity planning, what authority that participation carries, and whether plans recognize and address disproportionate harms. We identify that droughts/floods are associated with an increase in hardship; the likelihood that a household has enough shoes and clothes for all family members decreases by 3.0 and 2.2 percentage points respectively. item.description: Asian Journal of Advanced Research and Reports — Urban climate risks are produced through interactions between changing hazards, built form, ecological conditions, infrastructure and unequal social vulnerability. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), geographic information systems (GIS) and Earth observation now allow these interactions to be represented at increasingly fine spatial and temporal scales. item.description: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta) — During wildfire evacuations, timely action is essential to ensure life safety and minimize risk. As climate change increases the frequency and severity of wildfires, evacuation studies become necessary to improve emergency planning and ensure community resilience. However, temporal insights are not well-defined for wildfire evacuations due to data scarcity, resulting in a lack of time-based knowledge, especially for community-wide movement patterns. item.description: Earth stewardship. — Abstract In Hawaiʻi, wildfires represent an escalating crisis for communities, with growing impacts to health and human safety, native ecosystems, vital watersheds, and nearshore coral reefs. item.description: Research Square — Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) refers to particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 µm or less. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Climate change is escalating extreme weather, profoundly challenging global railways. UIC’s RERA (Resilient Railways) initiative addresses these threats through two reports: “Resilient Railways facing High Temperatures” and “Resilient Railways facing Heavy Rains”. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Flooding poses a major threat to urban transport networks, disrupting connectivity and access to essential services such as hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies. Assessing resilience is complicated by the differential exposure of roads to flood hazards and variable repair times. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Urban transport systems function as intricate interdependent networks encompassing road, rail, and public transit modes. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Floods are significant climate-induced natural disasters that frequently impact the resilience of urban areas, largely due to unplanned urbanization and increasing population density, which lead to inadequate infrastructure. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Public transport plays a key role in decarbonizing the transport sector, but in Sweden, the sector is challenged by a slow post-Covid recovery. item.description: Clean Technologies and Environmental Policy — Controlling vehicle emissions remains a critical challenge for improving urban air quality. Although multiple emission control strategies have been adopted worldwide, their main characteristics and outcomes remain scattered, hindering a systemic understanding of what works, where, and under which conditions. This study evaluates the empirical determinants of public compliance, behavioral adaptation, and enforcement friction using primary multi-stakeholder surveys and field environmental audits across five representative geographic zones. item.title: Cargo Bikes as a Resilient Transport Mode in Emergency Scenarios
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract In crises such as power outages, natural disasters, or security-related disruptions, mobility systems must function under decentralized and resource-constrained conditions. Cargo bikes offer a promising yet underexplored contribution to resilience. They require no fuel or license, involve relatively low costs, and can be operated without specialized training, which makes them accessible to both emergency services and communities. item.title: Designing Climate Resilience: A Policy Lab Approach to Climate Adaptation in Swedish Transport Systems
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Climate change increasingly challenges transport infrastructure, demanding adaptive governance across administrative levels. This project examines a design-driven policy lab involving four Swedish municipalities, a regional municipal association, and a reference group representing local, regional, and national authorities. Through facilitated exercises and tailored manuals, local officials identified barriers, mapped stakeholders, and jointly developed actionable adaptation strategies. item.title: Operational Resilience of Road Systems When Disruptions Arise
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Climate change driven hazards, including intense rainfall, flooding, and heatwaves, increasingly threaten road transport, disrupting mobility. As infrastructure age faster than they can be upgraded, the inability to respond swiftly to emerging threats results in cascading risks across the interdependent services like emergency response and healthcare. This research adopts a systems thinking approach to investigate how operational resilience of the road systems can be enhanced during such disruptions. item.title: Resilient Urban Logistics for Disaster Response: Evaluating the Valencia Living Lab in the DISCO Project
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract The València Living Lab was established in response to the flash floods of 29 October 2024, which caused 230 fatalities and severe disruption across key municipalities in the province of València. Developed under the EU-funded DISCO project, the Living Lab aimed to test a scalable, sustainable logistics model for crisis response through a combination of infrastructure reuse, digital coordination, and green last-mile distribution. item.title: Simulation Framework to Evaluate Link Criticality in Multimodal Freight Transport Networks Using Operational Metrics
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract Growing geopolitical risks and climate extremes have renewed interest in strengthening the resilience of transport networks to safeguard economic competitiveness and stability. A key step in network resilience planning is identifying critical components. While link criticality has been widely studied, freight networks present challenges due to their multimodal, multi-commodity nature. item.description: Discover Artificial Intelligence — The rapid advancement of Intelligent Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technologies has significantly expanded their role in modern public safety and security operations within emerging smart city ecosystems. item.title: Contribution of Cross-Analysis of Crowdsourcing Geospatial Data, Photographic Data, and Satellite Image to a Road Maintenance Strategy
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Abstract In low-income countries such as Madagascar, road infrastructure management is hindered by the absence of comprehensive databases and limited access to modern monitoring tools. This study addresses this challenge by assessing the quality of a main road network at the scale of a rural municipality in order to ensure territorial accessibility. The approach combines participatory science, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Remote Sensing to identify both the extent and condition of the road network. item.title: Health impacts of water risks through water-borne and vector-borne diseases in informal settlements in the Global South and India
item.description: Discover Public Health — Abstract Informal settlements concentrate overlapping water risks that undermine health, well-being and livelihood security. item.description: Geomatics Natural Hazards and Risk — Identifying natural hazard hotspots is essential for disaster risk reduction, yet comparing and aggregating heterogeneous hazards remains challenging due to differences in metrics, spatial-temporal scales, and data availability.
